assumptions: OFFLINE BY INSTRUCTION: another unit owns :8012 and :8014 is taken, so no request was sent and no server was contacted. Every number in SHAPE-SEARCH.md, the candidate tables, and this handoff is PREDICTED; the only MEASURED inputs are ENGINE-R1's anchors (cell A P1=325 at residue 5; cell D compact+50 = 322 at residue 16) and the byte counts computed offline from compile_turn (447 / 383 bytes, 53 / 42 words).

The card's stub instruction ('calibrate against full P1=325 residue 5 and compact P1=322 residue 16 after 50 pad') is mathematically inconsistent with any additive stub of this corpus's text: the 50 filler tokens cannot be free while the same two anchors require the compact form to be 53 tokens shorter. Rather than fabricate a tokenizer that appears to meet both, the unit reports three calibrations and their residuals (SHAPE-SEARCH.md section 2) and labels all three as hypotheses.

L=13 is carried from ENGINE-R1 as a MEASURED constant and used unchanged for every variant. A proportional re-scaling was computed and deliberately NOT applied: an append's cost is a prompt delta dominated by template framing, not a per-byte rate (the real encoder paid 13 tokens for 4 extra bytes where a per-byte stub pays 3 per byte). calibration_limits(L) names any L outside {13} as unmeasured.

The search compares cycle bills per compile-every-turn accounting (the engine's lifecycle, and the account ENGINE-R1's headline used). Breakeven turns for a warm held prefix are unchanged from ENGINE-R1 and not re-derived here.

choose_shape pads to target 2, and additionally to B-1 for variants already in the free band (r >= 33), because the law says a residue-63 shape with one token of avalanche margin is the cheapest legal one; that extra target is a candidate the law then accepts or rejects, never a forced move.
